label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, but was orphaned in infancy when her parents died of fever. At eleven years old, she was brought to Prince Edward Island to live at Green Gables with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert, who had originally intended to adopt a boy. Despite early mishaps caused by her fiery temper and wild imagination, she quickly won the affection of her foster parents and community. She formed a deep bond with her best friend Diana Barry and maintained a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe throughout her school years at Avonlea and Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's, she taught at Avonlea School and later pursued higher education at Redmond College in Kingsport, where she published short stories. Upon finishing her degree, she married Gilbert Blythe, moved to Four Winds, and eventually settled at Ingleside as a mother of six children.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan by his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, and began attending Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. From his arrival, he harbored a prejudice against female teachers and expressed hostilty and contempt toward Anne. He engaged in various pranks at school, including pouring water down a classmate's neck and placing a live mouse in Anne's desk. After Anne lost her temper and whipped him with a pointer for the mouse prank, Anthony's bravado broke, but the punishment unexpectedly earned Anne his respect. Following the incident, he began helping her carry her books to school and acknowledged that her discipline was as effective as a man's. When Anne eventually resigned as teacher, Anthony fought two pitched battles with other schoolboys to release his feelings.

label: Personality
value: Aunt Jamesina is sweet.
unit: Aunt Jamesina is sweet, open-minded, and cheerful, holding a broad and tolerant philosophy on life. She prefers comfort and simplicity over strict rules, allowing the young women under her care full independence. She possesses a keen sense of humor, often teasing others or lightly joking about her own past and suitors. Deeply compassionate, she holds a strong affection for cats and believes in treating animals kindly.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth. After her daughter got married and moved to the mission field, she was left living alone in a large house until Philippa Gordon invited her to Kingsport to act as housekeeper for Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa at Patty's Place. She accepted and brought along two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later agreed to take in Anne's cat, Rusty. During her time at Kingsport, she managed the home, mothered the students, and provided humorous advice through their college years. When the girls graduated and went their separate ways, Aunt Jamesina moved home, taking all three cats with her. Later, despite her fear of snakes, she traveled to India to visit her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina has a fear of snakes
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth. After her daughter got married and moved to the mission field, she was left living alone in a large house until Philippa Gordon invited her to Kingsport to act as housekeeper for Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa at Patty's Place. She accepted and brought along two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later agreed to take in Anne's cat, Rusty. During her time at Kingsport, she managed the home, mothered the students, and provided humorous advice through their college years. When the girls graduated and went their separate ways, Aunt Jamesina moved home, taking all three cats with her. Later, despite her fear of snakes, she traveled to India to visit her daughter's mission field.

They 'appeared out' at church together following their wedding, beaming with pride.

label: Personality
value: Captain Jim was high-souled.
unit: Captain Jim was a high-souled, simple-minded, and exceptionally gentle man who possessed a chronic habit of enjoying life and remaining cheerful. He was uncommonly deferential and chivalrous toward women, refusing to allow a bad word against any woman to be said in his presence. Possessing the natural talent of a born storyteller, he delighted in recounting his many seafaring adventures and discussing deep philosophical questions. He was also extraordinarily kind and generous, even starving himself to feed a passing stray dog.

label: History
value: Captain Jim was a lifelong sea captain.
unit: Captain Jim was a lifelong sea captain who spent decades travelling the world and experiencing countless adventures, including shipwrecks, mutonies, and pirate attacks. Over fifty years ago, he lost his beloved Margaret when she drifted out to sea and perished in a storm. He eventually retired from the sea to become the lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point. When Anne and Gilbert Blythe moved into the old house of dreams, Captain Jim welcomed them warmly and quickly became a cherished friend and regular visitor. He introduced Owen Ford, the grandson of his old friend John Selwyn, to his cherished handwritten journal, the "life-book." Together, Owen and Captain Jim collaborated to write a novel based on Captain Jim's life and his romance with Margaret. Shortly after receiving the very first printed copy of his published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse.

label: History
value: Thomas Carlyle Meredith is known as Carl.
unit: Thomas Carlyle Meredith, known as Carl, moved to the Glen St. Mary manse with his widowed father, siblings, and Aunt Martha. Passionate about collecting small creatures, he frequently brought bugs, frogs, and ants into the house and kept odd bedfellows like a young garter snake or a lizard in his pocket. While exploring with his family, he often investigated nature, such as ant-beds and dragonflies. After playing in a wet marsh, he suffered a severe sore throat, and on another occasion, he dropped a live eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, which shocked her and upset his father. When a apparent ghost frightened the children in Rainbow Valley, Carl bolted first; to punish himself for cowardice under the rules of their Good-Conduct Club, he spent hours sitting alone on a tombstone in a cold rain until midnight. This ordeal resulted in severe double pneumonia, though he eventually recovered through dedicated nursing and community support. Later, when his father prepared to whip him for the eel incident, the minister saw his late wife's eyes in Carl's face and could not go through with it. Before his father's wedding trip, plans were made for Carl to stay at Elder Clow's.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge as a young handmaiden, following in the footsteps of her three older sisters. Because of her sisters' legacy, Miss Lavendar dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth.' She welcomed Anne Shirley and Diana Barry to Echo Lodge and enthusiastically assisted in preparing for Stephen Irving's return and his eventual wedding to Miss Lavendar. Following the marriage, she moved with Mr. and Mrs. Irving to Boston. She later married an American bricklayer named Tom, returning to Prince Edward Island to attend Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant lives at Four Winds Harbor.
unit: Living at Four Winds Harbor in a brilliant emerald house, Cornelia Bryant quickly introduced herself to Anne and Gilbert Blythe upon their arrival. She formed a close friendship with Anne, frequently visiting her home, sewing garments for impoverished children, and offering outspoken commentary on community events. She strongly supported Leslie Moore through her severe hardships and initially opposed Gilbert's decision to treat Dick Moore. Later, after the truth about Dick was revealed and Marshall Elliott cut his beard, she agreed to marry Marshall, whom she had known for over twenty years. Thirteen years after her marriage, she remained a central figure in Glen St. Mary, taking in and adopting the destitute orphan Mary Vance. She actively managed church matters at the local Presbyterian manse and continued visiting and helping her friends at Ingleside.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned when their sick mother, Mary Keith, passed away. Marilla Cuthbert took the twins into Green Gables, where Davy quickly earned a reputation for non-stop mischief, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and hiding Dora in a pigpen. Under the patient guidance of Anne Shirley, Davy formed a deep bond with her, striving to improve his behavior and learn moral lessons. He began attending Avonlea school, sitting alongside Milty Boulter, and over the years gradually grew out of his extreme naughtiness. Following the death of his uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora's support, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. As he grew older, he developed a strong interest in farming and took on chores around the property.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen.
unit: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen working in his father's store during winters and sailing during summers. He became obsessed with marrying Leslie West, though she snubbed his advances. When his father held a mortgage over the West farm, Dick threatened Leslie's mother Rose with foreclosure until Rose pressured Leslie into marrying him. Following their marriage, Dick lived with Leslie and her mother on the West farm for a single winter. After Rose died in the spring, Dick grew tired of settled married life and went to Nova Scotia before embarking on a voyage to Havana on the Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick caught yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the events at Four Winds, though for twelve years his family and community mistakenly believed his cousin George Moore—who suffered an brain injury and loss of identity—was Dick.

unit: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen working in his father's store during winters and sailing during summers. He became obsessed with marrying Leslie West, though she snubbed his advances. When his father held a mortgage over the West farm, Dick threatened Leslie's mother Rose with foreclosure until Rose pressured Leslie into marrying him. Following their marriage, Dick lived with Leslie and her mother on the West farm for a single winter. After Rose died in the spring, Dick grew tired of settled married life and went to Nova Scotia before embarking on a voyage to Havana on the Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick caught yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the events at Four Winds, though for twelve years his family and community mistakenly believed his cousin George Moore—who suffered an brain injury and loss of identity—was Dick.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy are orphaned children.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy are orphaned children brought to Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert after their mother's death. Unlike her twin Davy, Dora is well-behaved, obedient, and causes very little trouble, though Davy frequently tricks her or drags her into mischief. She attends school in Avonlea, sits with various friends, and participates in Sunday School diligently. When Richard Keith leaves a trust fund for the twins, Marilla and Anne are able to keep them permanently at Green Gables. As she grows up, Dora proves to be very sensible, womanly, and helpful, eventually taking over Anne's old porch room when Anne gets married. By the age of seventeen, she has a suitor named Ralph Andrews.

label: History
value: Ellen West grew up in the West homestead
unit: Ellen West grew up in the West homestead with her family. In her girlhood, she had a romance with Norman Douglas, but it broke off after a quarrel, leading Norman to marry Hester Reese out of spite. Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, Ellen fell into deep grief and feared being left alone. She exacted a solemn vow from her sister Rosemary, sworn on their mother's Bible, that neither of them would ever marry and leave each other. Years later, when John Meredith began visiting their home and sought to marry Rosemary, Ellen held her sister strictly to her promise, refusing to set her free. However, after meeting Norman Douglas at a silver wedding party, Ellen resumed her own old courtship with him. Recognizing that she wanted to marry Norman, she sought Rosemary's release from their former vow. Ultimately, both sisters agreed to release each other, allowing Rosemary to accept John Meredith while Ellen prepared to marry Norman in a navy blue dress.

Years later, when John Meredith began visiting their home and sought to marry Rosemary, Ellen held her sister strictly to her promise, refusing to set her free. However, after meeting Norman Douglas at a silver wedding party, Ellen resumed her own old courtship with him. Recognizing that she wanted to marry Norman, she sought Rosemary's release from their former vow. Ultimately, both sisters agreed to release each other, allowing Rosemary to accept John Meredith while Ellen prepared to marry Norman in a navy blue dress.

label: History
value: Faith moved to the manse
unit: After moving to the manse in Glen St. Mary, Faith quickly bonded with the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley. Operating without strict parental supervision due to her father's abstracted nature and Aunt Martha's incompetence, Faith frequently got involved in innocent escapades that scandalized local gossips, such as dancing on tombstones or accidentally cleaning house on Sunday due to a mix-up in days. To clear her father of blame for the Sunday house-cleaning rumour, she boldly addressed the entire congregation during a church service. Soon after, she dared Walter Blythe to ride pigs through the village streets, further shocking the community. Hearing that Norman Douglas's absence from church was causing her father trouble, Faith visited him directly and persuaded him to attend services monthly. When her pet rooster Adam was killed by Aunt Martha to feed a visiting minister, Mr. Perry, Faith was devastated, but she retaliated by singeing the minister's coat-tail when he criticized her upbringing. Seeking comfort, she struck up a deep friendship with Rosemary West. After realizing how much trouble their heedless actions caused their father, Faith helped establish the Good-Conduct Club to discipline themselves. However, her impulsive generosity—giving her shoes and stockings to a poor girl—led to her attending Sunday School bare-legged, which caused another parish scandal. To defend her father, Faith published a candid letter in the local newspaper explaining the incident.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea school after a summer trip.
unit: When Gilbert returned to Avonlea school after a summer trip, he tried to get Anne Shirley's attention by picking up her red braid and calling her 'Carrots', leading Anne to break her slate over his head and hold a grudge against him for years despite his immediate apology. Although Anne ignored him, Gilbert kept up a fierce but good-natured academic rivalry with her at Avonlea and Queen's Academy, where he won the medalist award. After Queen's, he surrendered his offered teaching position at Avonlea to Anne so she could stay near Green Gables, prompting Anne to forgive him and become his close friend. Gilbert taught at White Sands before attending Redmond College, where he served as Freshman Class president, studied medicine, and graduated with high honors. After being rejected by Anne on his first marriage proposal, he suffered a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever before she ultimately realized her feelings and accepted him. Upon marrying Anne, Gilbert moved to Four Winds to take over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe, and later settled at Ingleside, where he raised six children while practicing medicine.

value: Mr. Harrison moved to Avonlea

He got into a heated dispute with Anne Shirley over her Jersey cow breaking into his oatfield, but after Anne accidentally sold his cow and confessed with a cake as a peace offering, the two became close friends. When a lightning strike killed Ginger, Anne came over to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea and reconciled with him, transforming his untidy house into a clean, orderly home. Over time, Mr. Harrison settled comfortably into community life, regularly attending church, supporting the minister's salary, and offering candid feedback on Anne's writing projects.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, joining their story club where she contributed very sensible stories. She studied for the Entrance examinations and attended Queen's Academy, earning honors in the domestic science course and getting her teacher's license. She began her teaching career at Newbridge, earning a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor before taking over the Avonlea school. Later, she taught out West on the prairies. While visiting Anne during a holiday, she proposed to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy, though Anne declined. Jane eventually met and married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy greyish Englishman who made millions in mines, moving with him to Winnipeg and taking a honeymoon trip to Europe.

label: History
value: After the death of Cecilia, John Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary
unit: After the death of his wife Cecilia, John Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary as the new Presbyterian minister, bringing along his four children and an elderly relative, Aunt Martha, to manage the manse. Due to his intense scholarly absorption and absent-mindedness, he frequently neglected household affairs and occasionally missed parish duties, such as prayer meetings and weddings. He formed a warm, unreserved friendship with young Walter Blythe, and eventually met Rosemary West by a spring in Rainbow Valley. Over the autumn and winter, he regularly visited her home, falling deeply in love with her. He attempted to propose to Rosemary, but she unexpectedly asked for time to consider before sending a written refusal, leaving him crushed and heartbroken. Meanwhile, criticism from parishioners like Mrs. Alec Davis forced him to confront his failures as a parent, though he found himself incapable of corporally punishing his children when they misbehaved. When his son Carl fell gravely ill with pneumonia, and later when Una fainted in church, his deep devotion to his children was painfully tested. Ultimately, after receiving a note from Rosemary inviting him to meet at the spring, their romance was restored, leading to their engagement and upcoming honeymoon.

unit: Josie Pye attended Avonlea school, where she frequently clashed with Anne Shirley and other classmates. label: History
value: Lavendar lived a secluded life.
unit: Lavendar lived a secluded, quiet life at Echo Lodge, an old stone house in Grafton built by her grandfather. After a youthful quarrel broke her engagement to Stephen Irving, she remained unmarried and occupied her time with imaginary tea parties and the woodland echoes across the river. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, quickly becoming close friends and bringing lively company back to her life. Anne later introduced Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to Lavendar, igniting her maternal feelings. Learning that Stephen was back in the area, Anne facilitated a meeting that reunited the former lovers, leading to their marriage at Echo Lodge. Following her wedding, she moved away to Boston with her husband, stepson, and handmaiden, returning to Echo Lodge for pleasant summer visits.

unit: Leslie grew up at Four Winds as the daughter of Frank and Rose West. When her mother was threatened with foreclosure by Abner Moore, Leslie sacrificed her own ambitions and married Dick Moore to preserve their home. Her mother died shortly after, and Dick went missing on a sea voyage to Cuba. Years later, Captain Jim found a brain-damaged man in Havana with a note from Leslie and brought him home; Leslie faithfully spent eleven years nursing him under the belief he was her husband.

label: History
value: Leslie formed a close, warm friendship with Anne.
unit: Following the arrival of Anne and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie gradually formed a close, warm friendship with Anne after overcoming initial feelings of envy and resentment. During the summer, she took in Owen Ford as a boarder, and the two fell deeply in love, though Leslie kept her feelings hidden due to her marriage. Later, Dr. Gilbert Blythe convinced Leslie to send the brain-damaged man to Montreal for a cranial operation. The surgery restored the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever thirteen years prior. Upon learning she was free, Leslie returned home and eventually accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage in Anne's garden, preparing to be married at Christmas.

label: History
value: Jem was born at the House of Dreams.
unit: Jem was born at the House of Dreams in Four Winds, named James Matthew after Captain Jim Boyd and Matthew Cuthbert. During his infancy, his family relocated to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, where he grew up alongside five younger siblings. As the eldest, he became a favorite of Marilla Cuthbert during visits to Avonlea, though he maintained a standing feud with Susan Baker over her insistence on calling him 'Little Jem.' He established himself as a leader among the children at school and in Rainbow Valley, where he frequently cooked meals, played games, and explored the natural surroundings. When the Meredith children moved to the Glen manse, Jem quickly befriended them and later suggested the creation of their Good-Conduct Club. As he entered his teens, he dedicated his time to studying for the entrance examinations to Queen's Academy, ultimately departing for Charlottetown to continue his education.

label: Personality
value: Marilla is a woman of rigid conscience.
unit: Marilla is a woman of rigid conscience, narrow experience, and practical sense. Reserved and undemonstrative, she initially mistrusts frivolity or excessive imagination and rarely displays deep emotion openly. Over the years, however, her temper and crispness soften into a warmer, mellower nature. Deep down she possesses a subtle sense of humor and a fierce, loyal love for her adopted daughter Anne.

label: History
value: Marilla lived at Green Gables
unit: Marilla lived at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew in quiet routine until they decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm. By a misunderstanding, Mrs. Spencer instead brought back an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley. Though Marilla intended to return Anne to the asylum, Matthew's gentle pleading and her own reluctance to hand the sensitive child over to the harsh Mrs. Blewett led Marilla to keep her. Over time, Marilla's strict discipline gave way to deep maternal affection as she raised Anne through her school days and Queen's Academy studies. Following Matthew's sudden death from heart failure and facing a threat to her own failing sight, Marilla planned to sell Green Gables until Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to stay home and teach in Avonlea. Later, Marilla invited the widowed Rachel Lynde to move in with her and adopted the young orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. Years later, she rejoiced when Anne married Gilbert Blythe, reflecting that it set right an old mistake of her own youth.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was born into a family.
unit: Marshall Elliott was born into a staunchly political family of Elliotts at Four Winds. Fifteen years prior to meeting Anne, he made a public vow during a fierce election campaign that he would not cut his hair or shave his face until the Liberal (Grit) party came into power. Because the Liberals suffered repeated defeats, he remained unkempt for fifteen years, becoming a well-known eccentric figure in the community. During this time, he maintained a friendship with Captain Jim and spent time cod-fishing. When the Liberals finally won the election, he immediately forced the local barber to trim his hair and shave his beard, startling his household and neighbors. Shortly after his transformation, he married Cornelia Bryant and moved into her house, where he planted trees, a spruce hedge, and a rose garden. When the plight of the orphan Mary Vance was brought to light, he investigated the situation over-harbour and agreed to take her into their home.

label: History
value: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian
unit: Mary Vance ran away from her abusive guardian, Mrs. Wiley, and hid in a barn without food for days until the Meredith children found her and brought her to the manse. Shortly afterward, Mrs. Wiley died, leaving Mary stranded until Mr. Meredith and Una helped arrange for Miss Cornelia Elliott to adopt her. Living with Miss Cornelia, Mary threw herself into household work, transformed into a clean and healthy child, and began attending church and school. She joined the circle of children playing in Rainbow Valley, frequently sharing ghost stories, gossiping, and lecturing her peers on improper behavior. She frequently spread dramatic horror stories about stepmothers to Una and Faith, causing Una great anxiety until the truth was cleared up. Over time, she became an indispensable helper to Miss Cornelia and a deeply cherished, if outspoken, friend to the Glen St. Mary children.

Living with Miss Cornelia, Mary threw herself into household work, transformed into a clean and healthy child, and began attending church and school. She joined the circle of children playing in Rainbow Valley, frequently sharing ghost stories, gossiping, and lecturing her peers on improper behavior. She frequently spread dramatic horror stories about stepmothers to Una and Faith, causing Una great anxiety until the truth was cleared up. Over time, she became an indispensable helper to Miss Cornelia and a deeply cherished, if outspoken, friend to the Glen St. Mary children.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Deciding to adopt a young boy from Nova Scotia to assist with farm work, Matthew drove to Bright River station only to find eleven-year-old Anne Shirley waiting instead. Despite his severe shyness around women and girls, he immediately took a liking to her talkative, imaginative nature during the drive home and silently advocated for keeping her. Matthew quietly supported Anne throughout her upbringing, buying her a fashionable puff-sleeved dress for Christmas and encouraging her studies. Over time, he suffered from heart trouble while continuing to work the farm. After Anne won the Avery Scholarship, Matthew suffered a fatal shock upon reading news of the Abbey Bank's total failure and collapsed on the doorstep. He was buried in the poplar-shaded Avonlea graveyard, where Anne continued to visit his grave regularly.

label: History
value: Norman Douglas courted Ellen West.
unit: In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West for two years before a sudden quarrel caused them to break off their relationship. In a fit of temper, Norman hastily married Hester Reese, whom he came to despise due to her meekness and lack of spirit. After declaring that a session member had cheated him in a cow transaction, Norman refused to attend church for twenty years, though he allowed his late wife to go. When Faith Meredith visited his home to ask him to return to church and contribute to the salary, Norman initially intimidated and insulted her until she returned in a fiery rage to rebuke him; admiring her spirit, he struck a deal to contribute a hundred dollars a year and attend church once a month. His return to church caused a major stir in Glen St. Mary, and upon seeing Ellen West there after twenty years, he fell in love with her again. He began actively courting Ellen and eventually gained her consent after persuading her sister, Rosemary, to release Ellen from a long-standing promise. Norman expressed immense delight and satisfaction when his marriage to Ellen was settled.

label: History
value: Owen Ford recovered from a severe bout of typhoid.
unit: After recovering from a severe bout of typhoid, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds to regain his health by the sea and visit the place where his grandparents had lived. While staying with Leslie Moore, he met Captain Jim Boyd and was inspired to write a book based on the old sea captain's life-book. During his summer at Four Winds, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, but maintained his silence out of respect for her marital status before returning to Toronto. After Leslie was freed from her tragic circumstances, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer and proposed to her in the garden of the little house. The two were married at Christmas and went on to have two children, Kenneth and Persis. He published a successful novel based on Captain Jim's life and later bought the old House of Dreams to serve as a summer vacation home for his family.

value: Paul Irving moves from the United States to Avonlea at age ten
unit: Paul Irving moves from the United States to Avonlea at age ten to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, on the shore road. During his school years, he creates imaginary companions known as 'rock people' and writes whimsical letters and compositions. He visits Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, where his resemblance to his father helps rekindle a romance that leads to his father Stephen Irving marrying Miss Lavendar. Following the wedding, Paul moves to Boston with his father, stepmother, and Charlotta the Fourth, returning to Echo Lodge for summer visits. As he grows older, he outgrows his imaginary companions, takes up football, and begins publishing poetry. At nineteen, he attends Anne's wedding at Green Gables before traveling abroad for two years of study.

label: History
value: Philippa meets Anne Shirley during her first days at Redmond College in Kingsport.
unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant during her first days at Redmond College in Kingsport, immediately taking a liking to them and bringing them into her social circle. During her college years, she struggles to choose between two beaux from home, Alec and Alonzo, while enjoying the attention of various suitors at college. She moves into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella, enjoying a happy household life there. During a summer break, she falls in love with the Reverend Jo Blake, standing firm against her mother's initial disapproval until her parents accept him. She marries Jo shortly after graduating from Redmond and later attends Anne's wedding at Green Gables.

unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant during her first days at Redmond College in Kingsport, immediately taking a liking to them and bringing them into her social circle. During her college years, she struggles to choose between two beaux from home, Alec and Alonzo, while enjoying the attention of various suitors at college. She moves into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella, enjoying a happy household life there. During a summer break, she falls in love with the Reverend Jo Blake, standing firm against her mother's initial disapproval until her parents accept him. She marries Jo shortly after graduating from Redmond and later attends Anne's wedding at Green Gables.

label: Personality
value: Mr. Phillips is a strict teacher
unit: Mr. Phillips is a strict, sarcastic, and unyielding teacher who frequently resort to whipping and public humiliation for discipline. He suffers from spasmodic fits of reform but is otherwise lax with order and prone to neglecting his younger pupils to focus on older ones. He can be quite obstinate and is easily distracted by his personal interests.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at the Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at the Avonlea school. During his tenure, he was known for maintaining poor discipline overall, frequently resorting to whippings, and neglecting the younger students to focus his energy on preparing the advanced scholars for Queen's. He openly paid court to one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, helping her with her lessons in the evenings and giving her gifts. When Anne Shirley joined the school, he publicly humiliated her by making her stand by the blackboard for displaying temper and later by forcing her to sit with Gilbert Blythe for arriving late. Following a school concert and the end of the term, his engagement in Avonlea concluded at the end of June. Upon his departure, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the school.

During his tenure, he was known for maintaining poor discipline overall, frequently resorting to whippings, and neglecting the younger students to focus his energy on preparing the advanced scholars for Queen's. He openly paid court to one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, helping her with her lessons in the evenings and giving her gifts. When Anne Shirley joined the school, he publicly humiliated her by making her stand by the blackboard for displaying temper and later by forcing her to sit with Gilbert Blythe for arriving late. Following a school concert and the end of the term, his engagement in Avonlea concluded at the end of June. Upon his departure, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the school.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard, forming a close circle of thoughtful, ambitious friends. After graduating, she taught at Carmody school before taking over her home school. During her time teaching, she contributed to the Avonlea Village Improvement Society by writing papers for their meetings and helped introduce her famous aunt, author Charlotte E. Morgan, to her friends. Later, Priscilla secured her father's permission to pursue a B.A. at Redmond College in Kingsport, where she boarded with Anne. During their second year, she and her friends rented Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, establishing a cozy home with Aunt Jamesina as their housekeeper. After completing her studies at Redmond, Priscilla married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated with him to Japan.

label: History
value: Rilla is the youngest of the Blythe children.
unit: Rilla is the youngest of the Blythe children living at Ingleside. One day, Susan Baker dressed her in fine clothes and sent her with a basket of strawberries meant specifically for Mr. Meredith or Aunt Martha at the manse. On her way, she encountered Mary Vance, who attempted to take the basket from her. When Rilla stood firm and refused to hand it over, Mary terrorized her by chasing her down the Glen street while brandishing a large dried codfish. Rilla fled in panic, accidentally dropping and ruining the strawberries, before stumbling into a mud-puddle. She was picked up and brought home crying by Miss Cornelia Elliott.

label: History
value: Rosemary West grew up in a traditional Episcopalian household.
unit: Rosemary West grew up in a traditional Episcopalian household at the old homestead on the hill near Glen St. Mary. When she was seventeen, she was engaged to Martin Crawford, who drowned when his ship was wrecked at the Magdalens. Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, her grief-stricken sister Ellen persuaded her to swear on their mother's Bible that she would never marry. Rosemary lived quietly with Ellen for ten years, staying close to home and eventually offering music lessons to local children. Her life shifted when she encountered the Presbyterian minister, John Meredith, by a hidden spring in Rainbow Valley; the two formed a swift, deep connection over shared interests in books and music. When John proposed, Rosemary felt forced by her solemn oath to turn him down by letter, causing both of them deep sorrow. Months later, Norman Douglas persuaded Ellen to release Rosemary from her vow so that Ellen herself could marry Norman. After Una Meredith came to ask Rosemary to marry her father, Rosemary sent John a letter requesting to meet at the spring, leading to their reconciliation and upcoming double wedding alongside Ellen and Norman.

Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, her grief-stricken sister Ellen persuaded her to swear on their mother's Bible that she would never marry. Rosemary lived quietly with Ellen for ten years, staying close to home and eventually offering music lessons to local children. Her life shifted when she encountered the Presbyterian minister, John Meredith, by a hidden spring in Rainbow Valley; the two formed a swift, deep connection over shared interests in books and music. When John proposed, Rosemary felt forced by her solemn oath to turn him down by letter, causing both of them deep sorrow. Months later, Norman Douglas persuaded Ellen to release Rosemary from her vow so that Ellen herself could marry Norman. After Una Meredith came to ask Rosemary to marry her father, Rosemary sent John a letter requesting to meet at the spring, leading to their reconciliation and upcoming double wedding alongside Ellen and Norman.

label: History
value: Royal Gardner was a student at Redmond College.
unit: Royal Gardner was a student at Redmond College whose studies were interrupted for two years when he accompanied his ill mother abroad. Upon returning to college, he met Anne Shirley in a park during a rainstorm by rescuing her with his umbrella and subsequently sent her flowers. Over the next two years at Redmond, he courted Anne devotedly, sending her poems, orchids, and violets, and introducing her to his family. After graduating from Redmond, he proposed to Anne in the harbor park pavilion where they had first met. When Anne realized she did not love him and refused his proposal, he expressed bitterness before parting from her. His sister Dorothy later noted that he was recovering from the heartbreak, as he had from previous romantic disappointments.

Oh, Anne, it’s hard.

label: Appearance
value: Ruby was a handsome girl.
unit: Ruby was a handsome, showy girl with large, bright-blue eyes, a brilliant complexion, and a plump figure. She had long, beautiful golden-yellow hair worn in braids, though she later wore it styled up in town. Before her death from consumption, she grew very thin, with pale, transparent hands, overly bright eyes, and hectically brilliant cheeks.

value: Ruby was cheerful.
unit: Ruby was a cheerful, merry, and good-tempered young woman who enjoyed the pleasant things in life. She was heavily preoccupied with young men and romantic attention, boasting frequently about her suitors. She was inclined to be sentimental and hysterical in frightening or emotional situations, such as when Anne fell off the roof or when Mr. Phillips gave his farewell speech. Towards the end of her life, she fought desperately to cling to life and feared death deeply, though she eventually passed away peacefully with a smile.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as part of the circle of girls attending Avonlea School. During her school years, she joined Anne Shirley's story club, participated in school concerts, and joined the Queen's Academy preparation class taught by Miss Stacy. After graduating from Queen's, she secured a teaching position at Carmody, where she was widely pursued by local admirers. Following an attack of lung congestion during the winter, she developed galloping consumption and had to give up teaching. Throughout her illness she maintained a defiant pretense of health, continuing to talk gaily of her admirers and social plans. Shortly before her death, she opened up to Anne Shirley about her intense fear of dying and her unfulfilled wish to marry and have a family. She passed away quietly in her sleep the next night and was laid to rest in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as Avonlea's first female schoolteacher. Upon taking over the school, she introduced novel educational activities such as Friday afternoon recitations, field days for studying nature in the woods, daily physical culture exercises, and composition writing. In November of her first year, she organized a Christmas concert with her students to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. She later formed an advanced class for students preparing for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy, offering them an extra hour of instruction after school. Though offered a teaching position in her home district, she chose to stay in Avonlea to see her Queen's class through their final preparation. She thoroughly drilled and guided her students, instructing them to rest and refrain from studying during the exam period. Following the end of the term, her pupils all successfully passed the Queen's entrance exams. In later years, she maintained her bond with her former pupils and was invited to attend social occasions at Green Gables.

value: > I like it when it stays on the roof. It doesn't always. I spent a gruesome night in an old country farmhouse last summer. The roof leaked and the rain came pattering down on my bed. label: History
value: Susan Baker was hired as maid-of-all-work at the little house in Four Winds.
unit: Susan Baker was hired as maid-of-all-work at the little house in Four Winds when Anne and Gilbert Blythe were expecting their first child. She quickly devoted herself completely to Anne, fiercely taking charge of the household and mourning deeply when Anne's firstborn died. Susan remained as the permanent housekeeper and moved with the family when they relocated to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. Following the birth of Anne's son Shirley, during which Anne was gravely ill, Susan cared for the infant with intense maternal tenderness and considered him her special baby. She faithfully managed the Ingleside house, cooked, knitted, defended the family against local gossip, and raised all the Blythe children.

label: History
value: Una grew up in Maywater
unit: Una grew up in Maywater before her father was called to minister at Glen St. Mary. After finding the runaway orphan Mary Vance hiding in an old barn, Una helped take care of her and comforted her in the manse garret. Overcoming her extreme shyness, Una went to Miss Cornelia Elliott to beg her to adopt Mary so she would not be sent back to an asylum. Una participated in the house-cleaning incident that inadvertently sparked parish scandal, and later took part in a voluntary fast as part of the siblings' Good-Conduct Club punishment, which resulted in her fainting in church. Terrified by Mary Vance's warnings about stepmothers, Una lived in fear of her father remarrying. However, upon overhearing her father's anguish over his unrequited love for Rosemary West, Una privately visited her mother's wedding gown in a closet for strength, then walked to Rosemary's house to ask her to marry her father. Upon delivering Rosemary's reply to her father, she successfully brought about their reconciliation.

label: History
value: Walter Blythe spent his childhood playing with his siblings and friends in Rainbow Valley.
unit: He spent his childhood playing with his siblings and friends in Rainbow Valley, a hollow near Ingleside that he helped name. He frequently read poetry aloud to the local children and shared imaginative stories, often enthralling or terrifying his audience. After being dared by Faith Meredith to ride a pig through the village, he reluctantly complied despite his humiliation. When a fellow student named Dan Reese insulted his mother and Faith, he overcame his fear of physical confrontation and engaged in a fierce fight, emerging victorious and forcing Dan to apologize. Following the encounter, he found the courage to visit the dentist to address a recurring toothache, realizing that anticipation of pain was worse than the pain itself. He also formed a close friendship with the local minister, John Meredith, with whom he shared his thoughts.
